newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan insurer panel divided over entry of banks.
newsitem.headline: Japan insurer panel divided over entry of banks.

text.p: Japan's Insurance Council, an advisory panel to the finance minister, said on Friday that it is sharply divided over whether banks should be allowed into the insurance business.

A key member of the panel told reporters that some members of the council were against a proposal to allow banks and trust banks to join the insurance business through subsidiaries by 2001 as part of Japan's "Big Bang" financial reform.
However some thought banks should be allowed to take over troubled insurance companies as subsidiaries.

The panel member said some members opposed allowing banks to start over-the-counter sales of insurance products, although some supported the idea on the grounds it would diversify the sales channels of such products and increase efficiency.

Another advisory council to the finance minister, the Financial System Council, said earlier on Friday that members of the council had agreed to propose allowing banks to engage in the insurance business and investment trust management business through financial holding companies.

Japan's Lower House of parliament passed a bill on Friday to lift a decades-long ban on holding companies. The bill will be sent to the Upper House for debate and is likely to be passed into law next month.
Both the Insurance and Financial System Council are scheduled to finalise their proposals in June to help Japan set a schedule for implementing its Big Bang reforms.
